Capability-pack runtime installer: interactive TUI provisioning of native runtimes before merge-install — Autoharness must actually install/upgrade external capability-pack runtimes/binaries, not merely compose their instruction/agent overlays. Provide an interactive TUI checklist before merge-install where users check/uncheck capability packs. For each selected pack, first scan for pre-existing installations, detect existence and installed version, then offer an appropriate per-pack action: fresh install, upgrade, retain/skip, or clearly report unsupported/unavailable installation. Coordinate provisioning of selected pack runtimes BEFORE the merge-install workflow so a new customer devbox becomes operational without expert tool-specific setup knowledge. Initial explicitly named native runtimes: backlogit, agent-engram/engram, graphtor-docs. UX and docs must make installation order explicit: provision selected pack runtimes before composing/merge-installing their harness overlays.

CURRENT GAP: deploy preflight only advisory-checks backlogit, engram, and graphtor-docs; it does not download, install, upgrade, pin, checksum-verify, or provision models.

OPEN DESIGN QUESTIONS (preserve for later Stage deliberation — do NOT silently decide): supported OS/platform matrix; authoritative package/download sources; version/channel policy; pinning, checksums/signature verification and supply-chain safety; user-local vs system install and elevation; PATH refresh; offline/proxy/customer-network constraints; embedding-model provisioning for graphtor-docs; rollback/partial-failure semantics; non-interactive/headless/CI equivalent to the TUI; idempotence; upgrade compatibility; licensing/consent; whether autoharness itself is bootstrapped before the runtime-provisioning phase while still ensuring pack runtimes precede merge-install composition.

OPERATOR INTAKE (2026-08-11, verbatim): "Consider implementing a DAG (Directed Acyclic Graph) to keep the agent from spinning in reasoning circles over the same information."

CLASSIFICATION (conservative, Stage): FEATURE/SPIKE CANDIDATE — not yet triaged, not planned, not harvested, and deliberately NOT associated with PR #325. Recorded as intake only per operator instruction.

CANDIDATE SCOPE (framing only, not a decomposition): bounded reasoning-state traversal; duplicate-state detection (recognising that a state materially equivalent to one already visited is being re-entered); cycle prevention (a DAG/visited-set discipline over reasoning states so revisits are structurally impossible rather than discouraged); and OBSERVABLE TERMINATION (the agent can demonstrate it stopped because a bound was reached or the frontier was exhausted, rather than merely appearing to stop).

WHY IT LIKELY NEEDS A SPIKE BEFORE A PLAN: the hard part is not the graph, it is defining reasoning-state IDENTITY — what counts as "the same information" — plus where the traversal boundary sits relative to existing agent step contracts, and how termination is made observable rather than asserted. Those are open questions, so this is a spike candidate rather than a ready-to-plan feature.

PROVENANCE NOTE (supporting evidence, not a decision): the PR #325 Stage sessions are a concrete motivating case — fifteen-plus review passes never reached a fixed point, and repeated fix-then-refalsify cycles were ended by operator authority rather than by any convergence property of the process itself.

STATUS: intake only. No triage, no routing, no planning, no harvest, no shipment association performed. [STAGE DARK-FACTORY RE-TRIAGE 2026-08-14 (P-017; route claude-opus-5/anthropic/high; append-only, all prior text preserved above)] TRIAGED -- CLASSIFICATION CONFIRMED AS SPIKE-FIRST; NOT PLANNED, NOT HARVESTED; ENTRY STAYS ACTIVE. Stage concurs with the conservative intake classification: this is NOT a ready-to-plan feature. The hard problem is defining reasoning-state IDENTITY (what counts as 'the same information'), where the traversal boundary sits relative to existing agent step contracts, and how termination is made OBSERVABLE rather than asserted. Those are open questions, so an impl-plan would be speculative and a plan-review could not meaningfully gate it. Not routed to a spike this session because a spike consumes the same operator-selection authority the other deferred capabilities are waiting on, and this session's eligible high-priority work (BED0DDED) was already unblocked by hard external evidence. RELATED PRIOR ART for whoever runs the spike: the existing circuit-breaker and escalation-protocol instructions already bound repetition by COUNTING attempts (stop conditions, 3-consecutive-failure escalation, 3-review-cycle limits) rather than by detecting state EQUIVALENCE -- the delta this entry proposes is equivalence detection and observable frontier exhaustion, which is exactly why it needs a spike first. Entry stays ACTIVE at MEDIUM priority. Unblocker: operator selection of this as a lead capability, then spike -> impl-plan -> plan-harden -> plan-review -> harvest. [STAGE DARK-FACTORY RE-TRIAGE 2026-08-15 (P-017; route claude-opus-5/anthropic/high; append-only, all prior text preserved above)] CLASSIFICATION RE-CONFIRMED AS SPIKE-FIRST -- NOT PLANNED, NOT HARVESTED, AND NO SPIKE RUN THIS SESSION; ENTRY STAYS ACTIVE AT MEDIUM PRIORITY. This is a third independent Stage triage reaching the same conclusion, and it was reached by re-examining the evidence rather than by deferring to the prior annotations. REVISED RATIONALE FOR NOT SPIKING (the 2026-08-14 rationale is superseded, not repeated): the prior annotation declined to spike on the grounds that a spike would consume the same operator-selection authority the other deferred capabilities await. That reasoning is WRONG and is corrected here -- a spike is a non-destructive, planning-only, Stage-owned instrument, explicitly within Stage's authority and explicitly permitted by this session's operator directive to spike as appropriate, so operator-selection authority is NOT the blocker. The ACTUAL blocker is evidentiary: the central open question is reasoning-state IDENTITY (what counts as materially "the same information"), and answering it requires observing instrumented agent runs to see which states actually recur. No such instrumentation exists in this workspace, and none can be produced by read-only inspection while the operator is AFK. A spike run under those conditions could only emit an unfalsifiable opinion about state identity, which would be speculation wearing a spike's label -- strictly worse than an honest deferral, because a PROCEED verdict backed by no measurement would then be treated downstream as a gate that had been passed. NAMED FIRST QUESTION FOR WHOEVER RUNS THE SPIKE (framing only, NOT a decomposition and NOT an authorization to harvest): the three candidate-scope elements are separable, and OBSERVABLE TERMINATION is the most tractable and is largely INDEPENDENT of solving state identity. This repository already bounds repetition by COUNTING (circuit-breaker instructions, the 3-consecutive-failure escalation protocol, the 3-review-cycle plan-review limit, and the Stage 20-task/3-failure stop conditions), but those bounds are ASSERTED in prose rather than emitted as machine-checkable termination evidence. The spike should therefore first determine whether a termination-record contract over the ALREADY-EXISTING bounds delivers most of the reliability benefit at a fraction of the blast radius, and only then decide whether duplicate-state detection and a full DAG/visited-set traversal are warranted. That question is answerable from repository evidence alone and is the recommended entry point. SAFETY NOTE FOR THE EVENTUAL IMPLEMENTATION (not a blocker for the spike itself): a mechanism that governs when agents stop reasoning is authority-expanding runtime behavior, so the implementation -- unlike the spike -- will require explicit operator consent regardless of how strong the spike's findings are. Entry stays ACTIVE at MEDIUM priority. Unblocker unchanged: operator selection of this as a lead capability, then spike -> impl-plan -> plan-harden -> plan-review -> harvest. [STAGE DARK-FACTORY RE-TRIAGE 2026-08-16 (P-017; route claude-opus-5/anthropic/high; append-only, all prior text preserved above)] SPIKE RUN THIS SESSION -- CONCLUSION DEFER (confidence high); NOTHING HARVESTED; ENTRY STAYS ACTIVE AT MEDIUM PRIORITY. This session did NOT repeat the prior deferrals: it executed the read-only, Stage-owned spike that the 2026-08-15 annotation recommended, on the specific question that annotation named as answerable from repository evidence alone. Findings artifact: docs/decisions/2026-08-16-observable-termination-record-spike.md (passes backlogit docs lint --profile authoring with zero findings). RESULT: the 2026-08-15 hypothesis is HALF-CONFIRMED AND HALF-REFUTED, and its recommended first slice is WITHDRAWN. Confirmed: (F1) every repetition bound in this harness -- circuit-breaker retry threshold, 3-consecutive-failure escalation, 3-cycle plan-review limit, Stage 20-task/3-failure stop conditions -- is asserted in PROSE ONLY; a token scan across src/, schemas/ and .github/ finds no machine-readable termination construct, and install-harness SKILL.md line 380 states the circuit-breaker cooldown is deliberately "rendered into instruction prose rather than parsed as machine configuration". (F2) a mature structured emission substrate already exists in src/autoharness/telemetry/ with an established degrade-open discipline. (F3) observable termination IS genuinely separable from the unsolved reasoning-state-identity problem. REFUTED: (F4) the blast radius is NOT small -- because the bounds live in prose, an emission contract can only be introduced by editing the constitution, circuit-breaker and escalation instructions plus the Stop Conditions section of every agent template and their templates/ counterparts, i.e. the core behavioural contract surface of every agent the product generates. (F5) DECISIVE -- there is no consumer, so emission would be write-only telemetry that yields the APPEARANCE of reliability rather than reliability. (F6) the motivating evidence (PR #325 fifteen-plus non-converging review passes; and four consecutive Stage sessions re-triaging these same entries to identical conclusions) is real but does not discriminate: neither failure was caused by missing termination EVIDENCE, both by the absence of an ENFORCED bound -- which is precisely the authority-expanding mechanism reserved for operator consent. NARROWED NEXT SLICE for whoever picks this up: pick ONE bound (the plan-review 3-cycle limit is best -- most mechanical, Stage-owned, and it already has a natural carrier artifact), ship the READER in the same slice or ship neither, keep it record-only and degrade-open per the record.py precedent, and do NOT attempt duplicate-state detection or a DAG/visited-set traversal until that has shipped and produced real measurements. Reasoning-state identity remains unanswerable from static repository evidence and was not attempted. SAFETY NOTE REAFFIRMED: any mechanism that GOVERNS when agents stop reasoning is authority-expanding runtime behaviour and requires explicit operator consent; F6 shows the enforcing variant is the valuable half, which makes that consent a hard gate rather than a formality. Session record: docs/memory/2026-08-16-stage-dark-factory-session.md.

Independent of the waza and witr intake entries - separate subject, no shared scope, no ordering dependency, and must not be merged into a shared covering feature without an explicit operator decision. [EXTERNAL / backlogit-owned; NOT an autoharness defect; NOT a 143-S blocker] backlogit checkpoint writer SILENTLY DROPS all but three `context` keys. Observed 2026-08-19 during Stage recovery on shipment 143-S. `backlogit_create_checkpoint` retains ONLY `context.shipment_id`, `context.feature_id` and `context.branch`; every other key is discarded — nested objects AND flat scalars alike, including keys such as `finding`, `evidence`, `verdict`, `pr`, `p0`/`p1` that ALREADY EXIST in older checkpoint JSON files on disk, so the on-disk corpus is not self-consistent with what the current writer accepts. EVIDENCE: checkpoint-20260819-221723.json was created with a rich context payload (blocker detail, PR number, reviewed HEAD, review counts, carried P2 list, preservation inventory); read-back from disk showed `context` containing `branch` only. A second attempt using an all-flat-string context (checkpoint-20260819-222114.json) lost the same keys, ruling out a nested-value serialization issue and confirming a hard key whitelist. SEVERITY DRIVER — the failure is SILENT AND DOUBLY MASKED: the create call returns `{"path": ...}` success, and `backlogit_get_checkpoint` subsequently reports `valid: true` on the truncated record, so neither the write path nor the validation path surfaces the loss. An agent that trusts either signal will believe it has persisted recovery state it has not. Consequence: `resume_hint` is in practice the ONLY durable free-text carrier in a checkpoint, which is a poor fit for structured recovery data and forces prose encoding of fields that should be queryable. WORKAROUND IN USE: material recovery context is written into `resume_hint` and mirrored into a circuit-breaker memory record under docs/memory/. SUGGESTED FIX: either persist arbitrary `context` keys, or reject unknown keys loudly at create time so the caller learns immediately — the current silent-accept-then-discard is the worst of both. See docs/memory/2026-08-19/circuit-break-stage-pr372-review-fix-143-S.md for the full observation record.
